title: [VSC-24] VS Code chat: prefer the general channel when auto-selecting, and dedupe CHANNEL_CREATED by id, matching JetBrains
description:
Filed by VSC-18 (task-43363b5d) from its adversarial pass over the epic diff.
1. Channel auto-selection differs between the clients (architect comment-41ad6014 on VSC-18). JetBrains (VSC-22, ChatChannelSelection.choose) picks the still-listed id, else the general-type channel, else the first listed channel. VS Code media/chat.js updateChannels picks channels[0] after deselectChannel(), and on first load. The two agree only while #general is the oldest channel. Port choose() to chat.js (prefer ch.type === 'general', else channels[0]) and mirror ChatChannelSelectionTest cases (b) through (f).
2. VS Code MoeDaemonClient case 'CHANNEL_CREATED' pushes the payload into state.channels without checking its id, and chat.js 'channelCreated' does channels.push. A repeated frame lists the channel twice. JetBrains MoeMessageDispatcher replaces by id (filter { it.id != channel.id } + channel).
definitionOfDone: chat.js selects the general-type channel when the selection is gone or on first load, else the first listed channel; a node:test runs raw chat.js in vm over cases (b) to (f) of ChatChannelSelectionTest.
A repeated CHANNEL_CREATED with a known id leaves one entry in the client cache and in the chat.js list, with a test (tests/wire-parity.test.cjs style).
In a git-archive snapshot, moe-vscode `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0.

Section D drives the RAW media/chat.js through loadPage() over JetBrains ChatChannelSelectionTest cases (b) to (f) (moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/ChatChannelSelectionTest.kt; case (a) is VSC-6's C3). Fixtures spread from CHAN_G/CHAN_X: SEL_GENERAL (chan-general, type general), SEL_GENERAL_2 (chan-general-2, general), SEL_ZETA (chan-zeta, custom), SEL_ALPHA (chan-alpha, name alpha, type role), SEL_GONE (chan-deleted, custom). Helper pageSelectingGone(list): loadPage(); updateChannels([...list, SEL_GONE]); clickTab(list.length). Tab order is general, epic, task, custom, then list order, so a custom channel listed last is the last tab. Then assert selectedInState() === 'chan-deleted' as a setup guard.
- D1 (b): pageSelectingGone([ZETA, GENERAL]), then updateChannels([ZETA, GENERAL]) selects chan-general: selectedInState, the last selectChannel post, and activeTabs() === 1.
- D2 (c): the same with [ZETA, ALPHA] selects chan-zeta (list order, not name order).
- D3 (d): a fresh page's updateChannels([ZETA, GENERAL]) posts exactly one selectChannel, chan-general. A fresh page's updateChannels([ZETA, ALPHA]) posts exactly chan-zeta.
- D4 (e): a fresh page's updateChannels([]) posts no selectChannel and shows 0 active tabs. A fresh page's updateChannels([GENERAL]) then updateChannels([]) leaves selectedInState null and exactly 1 selectChannel post.
- D5 (f): a fresh page's updateChannels([ZETA, GENERAL, GENERAL_2]) selects chan-general. pageSelectingGone([ZETA, GENERAL_2, GENERAL]) then updateChannels([ZETA, GENERAL_2, GENERAL]) selects chan-general-2.

Section E, CHANNEL_CREATED:
- E1 (withProvider, withSnapshot true): CHAN_Y delivered twice gives channelIds() ['chan-g','chan-x','chan-y']. Then {...CHAN_X, name:'x2'} gives ['chan-g','chan-y','chan-x'], and the last cache entry deep-equals that payload: the latest payload wins and moves last, like JetBrains `filter { it.id != channel.id } + channel`. h.posts deep-equals exactly the three {type:'channelCreated', channel} posts, so there is no updateChannels double-post.
- E1b (withClient plus snapshot [CHAN_G, CHAN_X]): a client.onChannelCreated listener records the JSON-copied cache ids at fire time. Two CHAN_Y frames record [['chan-g','chan-x','chan-y'], ['chan-g','chan-x','chan-y']]: the cache is written first, then the event fires, as in B1b.
- E2 (raw page): updateChannels([CHAN_G, CHAN_X]), then channelCreated CHAN_Y twice, then channelCreated CHAN_X. selectedInState stays chan-g, and listedIds() gives ['chan-g','chan-y','chan-x']. Call listedIds LAST, because it clicks every tab.
- E3 (raw page): updateChannels([]), then channelCreated CHAN_X. The selectChannel posts are exactly ['chan-x']; assert that BEFORE selectedInState, which throws while no state was saved. selectedInState is chan-x and chatInput is enabled. Then channelCreated CHAN_G leaves the posts at ['chan-x'], because a listed selection is kept, like JetBrains choose. listedIds gives ['chan-g','chan-x'].
- E4 (error handling): with a snapshot, the payloads null, {}, {id: 42}, 'chan-x' and [], plus a frame with no payload, each pass assert.doesNotThrow, leave the cache JSON unchanged and leave h.posts []. Without a snapshot, a valid frame does not throw and currentState stays undefined. Then a STATE_SNAPSHOT with no channels key followed by a CHAN_Y frame gives JSON.stringify(currentState.channels) === JSON.stringify([CHAN_Y]). Compare JSON text here, because channelIds() throws a TypeError, not an assertion failure, when the list stays undefined. On a raw page after updateChannels([CHAN_G]), channelCreated with channel undefined, null, {} and {id: 42} does not throw, and listedIds stays ['chan-g'].
Rules:
- JSON-copy every vm-realm array before deepStrictEqual.
- Never spell any project.json globalRails.forbiddenPatterns string in the test (the markup-injection DOM property is one of them). Read tabs only through clickTab, listedIds and activeTabs.

implementationPlan.description:
moe-vscode/media/chat.js, Edit tool only. The tests run this raw page script in node:vm, so the helper stays inside this file. Error handling: malformed input is a silent no-op, never an exception.
1) Next to deselectChannel, add one helper (for example autoSelectChannel()). When nothing is selected and the list is non-empty, it calls selectChannel with the first channel whose type === 'general' in `channels` array order, else channels[0]. Array order is the daemon's list order, never tab or name order. With a selection or an empty list, it does nothing. Comment it as JetBrains ChatChannelSelection.choose parity.
2) case 'updateChannels': keep VSC-6's lines byte-identical: `channels = data.channels || []`, the drop-unlisted branch that calls deselectChannel(), and renderChannels(). Replace only the old 'Auto-select first channel if none selected' block with the helper call. A still-listed selection stays and posts nothing (C3).
3) case 'channelCreated' (braced, for a block-scoped const):
- Ignore the message unless data.channel is truthy and data.channel.id is a string.
- Replace by id: channels = channels.filter(ch => ch.id !== id), then push the payload. The latest payload wins and moves last, as in JetBrains MoeMessageDispatcher `filter { it.id != channel.id } + channel`.
- Call renderChannels(), then the helper, since JetBrains runs choose() on every channel-list change.
- Never deselect here. channelCreated is not a full list, and a restored selection may arrive before the first updateChannels.
No added line may contain a globalRails.forbiddenPatterns string; build no markup. Prototype size: +19/-9.

implementationPlan.description:
moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts, case 'CHANNEL_CREATED' in handleMessage (line ~1682), Edit tool only. Mirror VSC-6's CHANNEL_DELETED block below it, and leave that block byte-identical. Wrap the case in braces.
- Error handling: const id = payload?.id; if typeof id !== 'string', break with no cache write and no event. JetBrains ignores an unparseable payload. Today a null or {} payload is pushed into state.channels, where it later breaks CHANNEL_DELETED's filter (c.id on null).
- Cache first: when this.state exists, state.channels = (state.channels ?? []).filter(c => c.id !== id), then push payload. A snapshot without a channel list starts one, as today. With no snapshot, nothing is cached.
- Then fire this._onChannelCreated once per valid frame, also with no snapshot. This is unchanged: ChatViewProvider posts channelCreated, and the page dedupes.
- Never fire _onStateChanged or _onChannelsReceived here. ChatViewProvider posts updateChannels for both, so the page would be told twice (mem:gotcha-vscode-wire-parity-test-harness point 9; E1 pins the exact posts).
No change to ChatViewProvider.ts or types/moe.ts. Prototype size: +11/-5, and it passes tsc -p and eslint.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: VS Code chat matches JetBrains in two places. (1) media/chat.js: when nothing is selected (on first load, after the selected channel leaves an updateChannels list, or when a channelCreated arrives with no selection), the page selects the first general-type channel in the daemon's list order, else the first listed channel, else nothing. A still-listed selection is kept and posts no selectChannel. (2) CHANNEL_CREATED replaces by id in the MoeDaemonClient cache and in the chat.js list: a repeated frame leaves one entry, and the latest payload wins and moves last. The cache is written before onChannelCreated fires. A payload without a string id is a silent no-op in both layers.
